doc.title: Alcide "Slow Drag" Pavageau and Lawrence Marrero Interview, 1957-09-01

title: Chord positions and playing guitar in the old days
summary: Allen asks if Marrero uses the chords in the book; Marrero says in jazz you play whatever works, notes early guitar had no extended chords, and shows alternate positions for F.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: And Lawrence, you've got a lot of second and third and fourth position chords in here. Do you use those very much? Use them all the time or what? Well at all the time.

At all the time. At all the time. At least sometimes. You see when I'm playing jazz, you just make anything. You make anything. No one can make it right. Just make anything. You can't look for all sorts of things like we, when you're playing, as I was saying, that's a guitar, I can look for a guitar too. Because I've never made a guitar play that I was playing today. When I'm playing guitar, we didn't make such a thing as those ninths, fifths, tenths, eleventh, thirteenth chords. We didn't make such a thing. We didn't have all that. No, we didn't have that. Most of it was the minor, the majors, the flats, you know what I mean. But now, a guitar player got a hard time.

Well when you say when you're playing jazz, make whatever you can, but make it right, first, second, third position, G seventh. If it's a G seventh, make a G seventh, wherever you can. Is that the idea? No, that's right.

That's right. That's right. Sometimes it may sound, you'll ever get to know how to make it in different places though, because, or a different position I'm going to say, in case you're playing, the band playing low, you know, or you can, the band's low, you can get low. When they're playing loud, you can get heavy too. You can make it loud too. Up there. Yeah. Now let's suppose you make F sound here. You can make F there. Well there's two ways they can make it. This one right here, even. And then you make F right here. Now I'm going to upset them right here, see that I play right here, I make it like in here. Yeah.
Let me get a big G. You're making F sevens? Yeah. Now I just put the frame down and make the, make what?
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Oh I see. That sounds like F natural here?
Now let's F again. There's something you're thinking wrong there.
You're thinking your C string in the fifth position. Also your G string in the fifth. Then you're thinking your D in the seventh. The D in the seventh.
Third string is in the seventh position.
And your A string in the eighth. Yeah. The bandages move louder than nothing. Oh yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
Yeah. That was a book that you'd like to practice on.
Now that's one of the books that you'd like to practice on one.
